libraries.triton_blockage_detail: triton 3.4.0 has no SDAA backend (only 'amd' backend dir). TensorLBM uses triton.jit kernels in _voxel_kernels.py for CUDA. compile_route.py documents that torch.compile on SDAA runs via teco_inductor (Torch-SDAA 3.1.1a3) whose backend is incomplete — L5 EXPAND assertion bug remains, so 'SDAA cannot compile this chain today'. Eager fallback is implemented.
libraries.verdict_reason: Extensive SDAA device support (1366 refs across 349 files, 35 benchmark files with SDAA refs, torch.device('sdaa:0') usage, torch.sdaa.synchronize() calls, _enable_sdaa_inductor() shim). However: (1) torch_sdaa not declared in requirements.txt/pyproject.toml, (2) triton SDAA backend absent — triton.jit kernels cannot run on SDAA, (3) torch.compile path blocked by incomplete teco_inductor (L5 EXPAND bug). Eager-mode fallback keeps benchmarks reproducible but compiled fast paths are unavailable.

libraries.triton_blockage_detail: triton 3.4.0 has no SDAA backend globally. TensorFEM does not use triton at all (zero triton references in .py files), so triton blockage is moot for this lib but still true at platform level.
libraries.verdict_reason: Zero SDAA references in entire codebase. No torch_sdaa dependency declared. No SDAA benchmarks. No triton usage. Library is torch-based but has no SDAA device awareness whatsoever.

summary.recommendation: TensorLBM is PARTIAL: has extensive SDAA device-level support and benchmarks but triton compilation path is blocked by missing SDAA backend in triton 3.4.0 and incomplete teco_inductor. TensorFEM and TensorBEM are BLOCKED with zero SDAA awareness. Priority actions: (1) Add torch_sdaa to TensorLBM requirements as optional dep, (2) Contribute SDAA backend to upstream triton or use torch_sdaa's own kernel compilation path, (3) Port SDAA device support patterns from TensorLBM to TensorFEM/TensorBEM once torch_sdaa is available.
